step1_analysis.description: A translinear attenuator circuit that exploits the exponential I-V characteristics of bipolar transistors to achieve a wide dynamic range. It uses an input voltage-to-current converter, a bipolar current mirror core for attenuation, and an output transimpedance amplifier.

paper_reference.title: A 147-dB Dynamic Range Electronic Attenuator for Audiometric Applications With On-Chip 1-W Power Amplifier

midband_gain.description: Voltage gain of the attenuator in its nominal (0 dB attenuation) state

sky130_expected.calculation: With R2 = R3 = 10k and a 1:1 current mirror ratio between Q1/Q2 and Q3/Q4, the transimpedance gain cancels the V-to-I conversion, yielding 0 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by resistor matching and BJT beta/Early voltage.

dynamic_range.description: Ratio of maximum output signal to noise floor

sky130_expected.calculation: Requires specific control voltage sweeping and noise integration over 20 kHz audio band.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Highly dependent on the noise floor of the op-amps and thermal noise of the 10k resistors.

thd.description: Total Harmonic Distortion for a 1 kHz input signal

sky130_expected.calculation: Simulated via Fourier analysis on the transient output.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Distortion arises from BJT base current errors and non-ideal virtual grounds.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power dissipated by the circuit

sky130_expected.reasoning: Scaled down significantly due to 1.8V supply and 10k bias resistors compared to the paper's 1-W PA inclusion.

sky130_expected.calculation: Limited by BJT parasitic capacitances and op-amp GBW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Modern BJTs and ideal op-amps in the testbench will yield bandwidths far exceeding the 20 kHz audio requirement.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure AC gain, bandwidth, transient response, THD, and DC power of the translinear attenuator.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Electronic Attenuator Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Generic BJT models for translinear core
.model pnp pnp
.model npn npn

* Parameters
.param R_val=10k

* Ideal Op-Amps replacing A1 and A2 from netlist
* A1 (N1 GND) amplifier -> Input buffer
E1 N1 GND VIN GND 1
* A2 (VOUT N4 GND) amplifier -> Output transimpedance amplifier
E2 VOUT GND GND N4 1Meg

* DUT (Original netlist with parameterized resistors)
Q1 GND GND VE1 pnp
R1 VE2 VEE {R_val}
R2 VE1 N1 {R_val}
R3 VOUT N4 {R_val}
Q3 GND GND VE2 npn
R4 VIN GND {R_val}
Q4 N4 GND VE2 npn
Q2 N4 GND VE1 pnp

* Stimulus
VVIN VIN GND DC 0 AC 1 SIN(0 0.1 1k)
VVEE VEE GND DC -1.8

.control
  * DC Operating Point
  op
  let power = abs(i(VVEE) * -1.8)
  print power

  * AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
  ac dec 10 10 100Meg
  let gain_db = vdb(VOUT)
  meas ac midband_gain find gain_db at=1k

  * Transient Analysis for THD and Swing
  tran 10u 5m
  meas tran v_max max v(VOUT)
  meas tran v_min min v(VOUT)
  fourier 1k v(VOUT)
.endc

.end
